page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-144 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 144 vCPUs mapped to 72 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 540 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. The processor includes a large 504 MB L3 cache, along with advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512).

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-144 demonstrates top-tier performance across multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic operations. Multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU scores, and PassMark database operations all rank in the top 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block transfers reaching 11,548.62 GB/sec and large block uncached writes reaching 213.92 GB/sec. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests placing in the middle 50%.

The hardware configuration delivers high resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require dedicated GPU hardware. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions enables top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing and medium-model text generation. This instance is optimized for large-scale database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
